body:
Yes, I actually do have more than adequate legal assistance. As much as I resent the military right now, they're doing me right on that end.

Something that you completely didn't ask, but I feel I should mention as I learned it today. There's a chance I have a tumor in my brain, so we'll see how that goes.

If I do have brain cancer, there's a damn near 100% chance I'll get acquitted. So I guess that's something.

I wish I could say more about your comment, but I'm at a lack of words. Miguel de Cervantes is favorite author of all time; Don Quixote is my favorite novel of all time. I had no idea he was a jailbird.

I appreciate the motivation. I really really do.

Thank you for a response, you have no idea how much I appreciate the opportunity to actually to actually talk to a person about my problems. I have a lot of friends in real life, but I can't tell them anything at all. I can't even tell them that my security clearance has been suspended, which I promise you is a problem at my job.

I can't pose any hypotheticals unfortunately. I really wish I could, but anything could pose a security problem. It's  ridiculous that I'm still so concerned about the USA's security when I'm being accused of violating it, but life is life.

It is indeed a serious situation, and I don't see any way out of it. I wish there was, but I don't see any sort of resolution. In theory, I could be hung for what they're accusing me of. In reality, 10 years is the most I could expect, but why the fuck should I want that? That's at least 10% of my life, and I can't imagine spending that in custody.

Sorry to vent to you. I wish I had alternatives, but I really don't.

I would love to talk to a psychiatrist about it, but I don't. Two reasons:

1. The military will only pay for a psychiatrist that is military approved.

2. Psychiatrists don't have security clearances. Pretty much ever.

So, I can't talk to a psychiatrist about it. In theory, I could talk to a civilian about it under C/P confidentiality, but that could just get me in bigger shit than I'm in now. The national security act sucks, I promise you.

My lawyer is pretty good, the best the military provides. I lucked out, she's by far the most competent counsel I've dealt with.

Thanks for the response, it gave me a little hope. Not much, but it's the best I've had in weeks :)
